name: TX-36
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean (R+12) in East Texas
Babin's overwhelming financial advantage ($911K on hand vs. under $6K for Hart)
Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 5% win chance
No polls or expert ratings point to any competitiveness
model.rationale: Every available signal aligns: the district's R+12 lean, Babin's incumbency and roughly forty-to-one cash advantage, and prediction markets pricing a Democratic win near 5%. With no polling or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, this sits firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: A sharp national political wave toward Democrats or a late influx of outside spending for Hart would be the main forces that could narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brian Babin seeks another term in this East Texas district, which carries a Republican partisan lean of about twelve points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised over $1.1 million and holding more than $900,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Rhonda Hart has raised roughly $24,000 and has under $6,000 available. No outside spending has been reported on either side.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about five percent, and no public polls or expert race ratings flag the contest as competitive. The fundamentals, money, and market signals all point the same direction, so the seat is rated Safe for Republicans, with the incumbent favored by a wide margin.
